sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2021 · Q76
sourceIssues.issue: Six pulleys in EACH block ordinarily give 12 supporting rope segments, so ideal rope tension is 3000/12=250 N and the downward ground thrust of a man pulling down is 650−250=400 N, absent from the choices. A total of six supporting segments would give 150 N (C). The printed wording and choices disagree.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2026 · Q1
sourceIssues.issue: For a quarter-circle area, x̄=ȳ=4R/(3π), corresponding to D for either Cartesian coordinate. The distance along its symmetry line from the corner is √(x̄²+ȳ²)=4√2R/(3π), which is not listed. The question explicitly asks for the distance on the symmetry line; automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2018 · Q70
sourceIssues.issue: With the stated applied force of 100 N, actual static friction is 100 N (C). The limiting friction at impending motion is μN=0.5×1000=500 N (D), but a 100 N pull cannot cause that impending state. The wording conflates actual and limiting friction; automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: GATE XE-D 2009 · Q12
sourceIssues.issue: The printed geometry is inconsistent: a tangent at 30° with centre-to-hinge distance 5 m requires radius 5sin30°=2.5 m, whereas the figure labels radius 1 m. Using the stated angle and distance gives ω=10tan30°/5=1.155 rad/s (B). Using radius 1 m and distance 5 m instead gives θ=asin(1/5) and ω≈0.408 rad/s. The conflict is explained rather than automatically graded.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2024 · Q71
sourceIssues.issue: The printed mass is given in kN, a force unit. Taking 3 kN as weight: m=3000/9.81 kg, I=mk²=782.875 kg·m². Energy increase = ½I[(340π/30)²−(315π/30)²]≈70.29 kJ; final stored energy≈496.23 kJ. Neither appears in the options. Treating 3 as tonnes also fails to match the printed choices.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 1999 | Archive Book Q1.7
sourceIssues.issue: The printed key lists alternative letters A, C for a single-choice question. This is not a multi-select format. Review the source alternatives; automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2024 · Q25
sourceIssues.issue: The exact property described is elasticity: recovery of original shape when load is removed. Resilience (B) is related but specifically concerns elastic energy absorption and release. Elasticity is absent from the options, so B should not be presented as an unqualified exact definition.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2020 · Q95
sourceIssues.issue: The supplied book gives D. With Griffith σf=√(2Eγ/πa), interpreting the stated 100 μm as total internal-crack length 2a gives 163.5 MPa, nearest D (160 MPa). Interpreting it as the half-length a gives 115.6 MPa, nearest B (120 MPa). The stem does not specify crack geometry or this convention, so both interpretations are shown and automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2004 | Archive Book Q6.17
sourceIssues.issue: Mild steel is used for commercial beams (A→2), and tool steel for blanking dies (B→4), selecting option A. The remaining printed associations are medium-carbon steel→screws and high-carbon steel→crane hooks; the latter is not a good general materials-selection recommendation (hooks normally require tough low/medium-carbon steel). The printed book key D also incorrectly assigns mild steel to hooks and high-carbon steel to beams. Because the source matching list itself is defective, automatic grading is withheld; A is the structurally intended match, not an endorsement of every pairing.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Q82
sourceIssues.issue: Nickel-based superalloys have excellent creep resistance (3 true). Vitallium is cobalt-based, not vanadium-based (2 false). Discalloy and conventional Incoloy are iron–nickel-based rather than simply nickel-based, so the second clause of statement 1 is inaccurate. The apparent intended choice is C (1 and 3), but strictly only 3 is true and that choice is absent.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 1999 | Archive Book Q5.8
sourceIssues.issue: The printed key lists alternative letters B, C for a single-choice question. This is not a multi-select format. Review the source alternatives; automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2007 | Archive Book Q5.24
sourceIssues.issue: The printed book key indicates D (Pyrosil). Alumina and porcelain are ceramics. A whisker is a single-crystal reinforcement morphology and may itself be ceramic (such as SiC or Al₂O₃), metallic or another material; the generic word does not uniquely specify a material class. Pyrosil is a commercial name whose composition is not specified here. Because the terminology is insufficient for an unambiguous independent classification, the printed answer is retained as a reference and automatic grading is withheld.

sourceIssues.title: ESE Prelims 2019 · Q91
sourceIssues.issue: Griffith fracture for an internal crack of half-length a=2 μm gives σf=√(2Eγ/(πa))=√[2×70×10⁹×1/(π×2×10⁻⁶)]≈149.27 MPa. None of 885, 895, 915 or 935 MPa matches the printed data.

sourceIssues.title: GATE XE-C 2009 · Q23
sourceIssues.issue: Aluminium supplies three valence electrons per atom in the free-electron model. Atomic density=ρNA/M=6.05×10²⁸ m⁻³, so electron density is 1.815×10²⁹ m⁻³, absent from the options. Option A instead assumes one conduction electron per atom. Automatic grading is withheld for this missing-assumption/source error.

sourceIssues.title: GATE XE-C 2009 · Q24
sourceIssues.issue: Drude conductivity σ=ne²τ/me. With the physically standard three electrons per Al atom, n=1.815×10²⁹ m⁻³ gives σ≈1.02×10⁸ S/m, absent from the options. Using the preceding question's apparent one-electron assumption gives 3.40×10⁷ S/m (C). This linked source ambiguity is excluded from automatic grading.
